newsitem.title: UK: News Corp to press ahead with ASkyB - FT.
newsitem.headline: News Corp to press ahead with ASkyB - FT.

text.p: News Corp will push ahead with plans to launch a U.S. satellite television operation next year despite the intention of partner MCI Communications to reduce its involvement, the Financial Times said on Thursday.

News Corp chairman Rupert Murdoch told the Financial Times that he was now considering three options for American Sky Broadcasting (ASkyB) - pushing ahead on his own with MCI as a minority shareholder, bringing in a new partner, or launching a share issue to raise more money for the venture.
Murdoch said he was under no pressure over the funding of the venture. "We have $3 billion in the bank," he said.

MCI, which on Sunday announced a $20 billion merger with British Telecommunications Plc, said it planned to cut its stake in ASkyB from 50 to 20 percent. It also said it would sell to Murdoch a $700 million satellite licence if it could.

MCI has a stake of just under nine percent in News Corp and has an option to raise this to 13.5 percent. But MCI chief executive Bert Roberts told Reuters on Sunday that it was unlikely to increase its stake.
The Financial Times said that Murdoch had conceded that the MCI shares in News Corp would have to be sold if they turned out to be a regulatory problem blocking the BT-MCI deal.
Britain's Oftel telecommunications watchdog recently suspended a joint marketing campaign between BT and BSkyB, the UK pay TV operator in which News Corp is the leading shareholder.
"There is a Mr Cruickshank (Oftel director general Don Cruickshank) who takes a great interest in what BT or Sky do," Murdoch said.
